title: Cohomology along an affine morphism: the edge map is an isomorphism
statement: Let $h:X\to S$ be an affine morphism of schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism] (for instance a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]) and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Then $R^ph_*\mathcal F=0$ for $p>0$ [pqf-def-cohomology], and for every $p\ge0$ the edge map $e_{h,\mathcal F}:H^p(S,h_*\mathcal F)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (c) (the map induced by the $h$-map $\mathrm{id}_{h_*\mathcal F}$) is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_S(S)$-modules.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 089W (lemma-relative-affine-cohomology, line 202) and its proof: Lemma 01XC (lemma-relative-affine-vanishing, line 181) and the Leray spectral sequence, Cohomology, Lemma 01F4 (cohomology-lemma-apply-Leray) part (1), whose identification is the edge map of Equation 01FA; used in Lemma 02OD's proof ('By the Leray spectral sequence for i_n')

proof.text: Apply the proved isZero_higherDirectImage_of_isAffineHom to h and F in every positive degree (lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi). The ringed-space moduleDirectImage of the scheme map is definitionally Scheme.Modules.pushforward h, so this gives the first assertion unchanged and shows that F is pushforward h-rightAcyclic.

Work with the actual resolution choices D used by moduleCohomologyEdgeMap (def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap). Apply Functor.quasiIso_map_of_rightAcyclic_nat (lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity) to D.I.ι and pushforward h. The source single complex has F in degree zero and zero elsewhere, hence all its terms are pushforward-acyclic by step 1. The terms of D.I are injective, hence pushforward-acyclic. Pushforward preserves finite limits since it is right adjoint to module pullback. Thus pushforward(D.I.ι) is a quasi-isomorphism. Precompose with the inverse of Mathlib singleMapHomologicalComplex to obtain α : single₀(h_*F) → h_*I. The defining compatibility for D.β gives D.J.ι ≫ D.β = α ≫ D.lambda: equality of maps from a single complex is checked in degree zero using CochainComplex.fromSingle₀Equiv. Since α, D.lambda and D.J.ι are quasi-isomorphisms, two-out-of-three makes D.β a quasi-isomorphism. This is the proved private helper beta_quasiIso.

proof.text: Apply quasiIso_map_of_rightAcyclic_nat again, this time to D.β and the additive left exact functor Γ(S,-) followed by forgetting to abelian groups. Both D.J and D.K have injective terms, so all terms are acyclic for this functor. Hence Γ(S,D.β) is a quasi-isomorphism and its degree-p homology map is invertible. Unfold D.map: its other factors are the injective-resolution comparison isomorphisms, the forgetful homology comparison isomorphisms, and the inverse of the homology map whose invertibility is the field D.invertible p. A composition of these isomorphisms is an isomorphism. This proves invertibility of the actual edge map in every degree without changing choices.

proof.text: Use the linearity clause of moduleCohomologyFMap_basic_properties for the identity h-map. Obtain a Γ(S,top)-linear morphism L into cohomology on X with scalars restricted along h.appTop. Rewrite the edge map as the underlying additive map of L and apply L.hom.map_smul. The restricted scalar action is definitionally multiplication through h.appTop, giving exactly the stated equality. Combine with steps 1 and 3 using conjunction introduction.

lean.statement: theorem affine_morphism_cohomology_edge {X S : Scheme.{v}} (h : X ⟶ S) [IsAffineHom h] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] : (∀ (p : ℕ), 0 < p → IsZero (((RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage h.toLRSHom.toShHom).rightDerived p).obj F)) ∧ (∀ (p : ℕ), IsIso (moduleCohomologyEdgeMap h F p) ∧ ∀ (r : Γ(S, ⊤)) (x : (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology S.toRingedSpace p).obj ((pushforward h).obj F)), moduleCohomologyEdgeMap h F p (r • x) = h.appTop r • @id ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p).obj F) (moduleCohomologyEdgeMap h F p x))
lean.note: Positive right-derived module direct images vanish; the recorded identity h-map edge map is invertible and compatible with global-section scalars through h.appTop. No derived-category choices are required.
